clue.text: She's a tender beauty, possibly, lacking years

indicators.note: possibly says the letters of the phrase a tender beauty may be rearranged into another word
lacking says some letters must be taken away from that phrase before rearranging

parts.note: the letters of the word year are what go missing from the pool

explanation.surface: A gentle beauty, perhaps, who is still young.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' and 'lacking' together make a composite anagram: take the thirteen letters of 'a tender beauty', remove the letters of YEAR, and rearrange the nine left.
explanation.definitionFit: A debutante is a young woman making her first appearance in society, so 'she' is a fair, if minimal, pointer.

indicators.note: in says the letter for united goes inside the word for kit

parts.note: kit is clothing or outfit, a dress
U is the standard abbreviation for united, as in football club names

explanation.surface: A team feeling the strain while wearing the club strip.
explanation.definitionFit: Duress is coercion or compulsion, pressure applied to force someone to act.

clue.text: Foreign capital is a Blair disaster

indicators.note: disaster suggests the words is a Blair have been wrecked and must be rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: A political jibe that some overseas capital city was a fiasco for Tony Blair.
explanation.walkthrough: Blair is the former British Prime Minister Tony Blair.
explanation.definitionFit: Brasilia is the purpose-built capital city of Brazil, so foreign to a British solver.

indicators.note: leader picks out the opening letter of the word Tory

parts.note: was upset in the sense of having been unwell or out of sorts, ailed

explanation.surface: A stubborn Conservative chief who was distressed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dogged' looks like an adjective meaning stubborn but is the past tense of the verb: followed closely.
explanation.definitionFit: To dog someone is to follow them, the same as to tail them.

parts.note: to bag something is to catch or net it
a lady is a woman, her; the 's stands for is, a link

explanation.surface: A homeless woman's shopping bag, apparently, belongs below ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bag lady' reads as one phrase; split it into the verb 'bag' and 'lady'.
explanation.definitionFit: Nether means lower or beneath, as in the nether regions below ground.

clue.text: Catch up taking catches in covers

indicators.note: taking says the outer piece holds the other piece inside it
up, in a down clue, says the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to catch someone's meaning is to see it
clips are fastenings, catches

explanation.surface: A fielder holding catches while wearing protective covers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Catch' is read as understanding, as in 'I catch your drift'; 'up' in a down clue turns it upward, and 'taking' wraps the result round the catches.
explanation.definitionFit: To eclipse something is to obscure or block it from view, as the moon blocks the sun.

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for ace on playing cards
a ward is a young person under a guardian's care, here a pupil; the 's is a link

explanation.surface: A star student wins a scholarship.
explanation.definitionFit: An award is a sum given officially, the same as a grant of money.

parts.note: a jumbo is a big airliner, which shows its speed in the sky through which it flies; also split as the pace of the air

explanation.surface: Asking where an elephant might reveal how fast it is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jumbo' suggests an elephant, but here it is a jumbo jet.
explanation.definitionFit: Airspace is the part of the sky above a country through which aircraft fly.

parts.note: AD, anno Domini, marks the present era, so today
a rift is a split or crack; the 's stands for is, a link

explanation.surface: Someone announcing that a split means they are now released.
explanation.definitionFit: Adrift means floating loose, untied, so free of moorings.

clue.text: Worn the same clothes every day, initially

parts.note: do, short for ditto, means the same
gear is clothing, as in sports gear

indicators.note: initially takes the opening letters of every and day

explanation.surface: Someone who wears the same outfit day after day.
explanation.walkthrough: DO, short for ditto, is a crossword convention for 'the same'.
explanation.definitionFit: Dog-eared describes pages or things with corners turned down, shabby from use, so worn.

clue.text: He's pragmatic about American leader's agenda

parts.note: re means about or concerning

indicators.note: leader picks out the opening letter of American

parts.note: an agenda is a list of items to cover

explanation.surface: A practical man discussing a US president's political plans.
explanation.definitionFit: A realist is a person who takes a practical, pragmatic view of things.

parts.note: the locks are not on doors but of hair, held in place by a clip

explanation.surface: A security device that keeps door locks safe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'locks' wants to be door fastenings; they are tresses of hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A hair slide is a clip that holds hair in place, called a barrette in the US.

clue.text: Harder military man's insides turned over

indicators.note: the inner pair of letters in the word for a military man swap places

parts.note: a soldier is a military man

explanation.surface: A tough soldier whose guts are churning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'insides turned over' turns DI, inside SOLDIER, into ID.
explanation.definitionFit: Solider is the comparative of solid, firmer or harder.

indicators.note: Head of picks out the first letter of state's

parts.note: the Mad Hatter of Alice in Wonderland makes hatter a crossword madman

explanation.surface: Outrage that a country's leader is insane.
explanation.definitionFit: To shatter someone is to devastate or shock them.

indicators.note: abnormally says the letters of can tailor bodies are arranged in an unusual way

explanation.surface: A drug that can reshape bodies unnaturally, as bodybuilders know.
explanation.definitionFit: An anabolic steroid is a synthetic hormone used to build muscle, a performance-enhancing drug.

indicators.note: last picks out the final letter of the word child's

parts.note: an option is a choice

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a child's final option is to be taken in by a new family.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of child's is read as possessive, so the last letter is D.
explanation.definitionFit: Adoption, being taken into a new family, can be the final choice open for a child without parents.

parts.note: something over is finished and done with, forgotten
lays are songs or ballads

explanation.surface: Cover versions of old songs nobody remembers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Covers' suggests cover versions of songs; it is a noun for things laid over others.
explanation.definitionFit: Overlays are layers placed on top of something, so covers.

clue.text: Chinese character Mao moved with terrible dirge

indicators.note: moved, together with terrible, says the letters of Mao and the dirge are churned up into one new word

explanation.surface: Chairman Mao is stirred by a dreadful funeral song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moved with terrible' signals the anagram: MAO and DIRGE are shuffled together as one pool of letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An ideogram is a written symbol standing for an idea, as Chinese characters do.

parts.note: out means not allowed, unacceptable, as in that idea is out
the right is the political wing opposing change, reactionary

explanation.surface: A damning verdict on an extreme right-winger.
explanation.definitionFit: Outright means entirely, wholly, so completely.

parts.note: OB is short for old boy, a former pupil; the 's is a link
an exhibition of temper or bad behaviour is a scene

explanation.surface: An elderly man's indecent display.
explanation.definitionFit: Obscene means offensive or indecent, as dirty jokes are.

clue.text: Backbone holding you, say, having no backbone

indicators.note: holding says the word for backbone wraps round the other piece

parts.note: the backbone is the spine

indicators.note: say signals the letter that is pronounced like the word you

parts.note: the letter U is pronounced the same as the word you

explanation.surface: A spine supporting someone, who is nonetheless spineless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backbone' appears twice: first as the spine, then figuratively as courage.
explanation.definitionFit: Supine means passive and weak-willed, lacking the courage of a firm character.

clue.text: A king stung by queen's authority

parts.note: R is short for rex, Latin for king
bit means stung, as an insect does
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen; the 's is a link

explanation.surface: A monarch is bitten, which is the queen's ruling.
explanation.definitionFit: An arbiter is a person with power to judge, an authority on a matter.

indicators.note: novel, meaning new, says the letters are formed into something fresh
lacking says a letter is removed from the name Thoreau

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A book by Thoreau that falls flat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like a book but is the anagram signal; take E out of THOREAU and shuffle THORAU. The whole clue doubles as a description: Thoreau was a writer.
explanation.definitionFit: Henry David Thoreau, who wrote Walden, was a writer, so the clue as a whole points at one.

indicators.note: penned means enclosed, so the answer is held within the words number, lines

explanation.surface: A songwriter has written the words of a musical number.
explanation.walkthrough: Irving Berlin wrote songs such as White Christmas.
explanation.definitionFit: Irving Berlin was an American songwriter, a composer of popular standards.

clue.text: Sat on the throne, we hear, and came down

indicators.note: we hear signals the answer is pronounced like the word given by the preceding phrase

parts.note: a monarch who sat on the throne reigned

explanation.surface: A monarch who ruled and then descended.
explanation.definitionFit: Rain comes down from the sky, so it rained means it came down.

definitions.meaning: the top level of any sport or profession, the best
the uppermost set of stairs sits right next to a landing

explanation.surface: A premium-class passenger nearing touchdown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'landing' suggests an aircraft touching down; it is the floor at the head of a staircase.
explanation.definitionFit: A top-flight player is among the very best, and the uppermost staircase in a house ends at a landing.

clue.text: Gas ring, for example, back on with nitrogen

parts.note: a halo is a ring of light

indicators.note: back says the abbreviation for for example is read in reverse

parts.note: eg is the abbreviation for exempli gratia, for example
N is the chemical symbol for nitrogen

explanation.surface: A gas ring, say, turned back on together with nitrogen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gas ring' reads as a cooker burner; 'Gas' is the definition and 'ring' starts the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Halogens such as chlorine and fluorine are a group of chemical elements, several of them gases.

indicators.note: say signals the answer is pronounced like the word for pounds

parts.note: a baker kneads or pounds dough

explanation.surface: Someone in urgent want of money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pounds' suggests money; it is the verb, as in pounding dough.
explanation.definitionFit: To need something is to require it badly, to be desperate for it.

indicators.note: on, in an across clue, says one piece follows the other

parts.note: a marina is a harbour for yachts, a port
Ted is a short form of the name Edward

explanation.surface: A man named Edward drunk on port wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soused' and 'port' suggest drinking; soused also means steeped in liquid, and port is a harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: Soused can mean pickled or soaked in brine or vinegar, which is what marinated food is.
